V. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE The Contractor shall provide to the U.S. Government the deliverables described in the Technical Specifications (Section I) of this Statement of Work. Further, the Contractor shall properly perform SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED 9 SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS all required testing, quality assurance, and validation on each Taskprior to submission for Government review. The final inspection and acceptance of ALL deliverables shall be performed by the U.S. Government upon completion and submission of the entire scope of work (Products 1 through 4). If INL Guatemala officials identify an incomplete, non- functional, or defective deliverable, they shall immediately refrain from accepting it and notify the Contractor in writing. Upon notification, the Contractor shall correct or replace the deficient deliverable at no additional cost to the Government. required for Task 3 (Production Deployment and User Acceptance Testing) and Task 4 (Knowledge Transfer). All coordination visits, deployment activities, and knowledge transfer sessions requiring physical presence shall take place at the GIO's institutional facilities in Guatemala City, Guatemala, as coordinated with the designated INL Guatemala point of contact. Remote work shall be permitted for all other tasks and activities where physical presence is not explicitly required, provided the Contractor maintains effective communication and coordination with INL Guatemala POC and the GIO throughout the period of performance. QUALITY ASSURANCE AND SURVEILLANCE PLAN (QASP) This plan provides an effective method to promote satisfactory contractor performance. The QASP provides a method for the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to monitor Contractor performance, advise the Contractor of unsatisfactory performance, and notify the Contracting Officer of continued unsatisfactory performance. The Contractor, not the Government, is responsible for management and quality control to meet the terms of the contract. NATIONAL INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AUTHORITY – UGANDA (NITA-U)

 

 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET)

PROJECT ID: P171305

LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/00027

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The con

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capability and experience is:

 

The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are:

Rationale 1.1 Compliance with Terms of Reference’s Requirements - Mandatory The Economic Operator shall submit a narrative of approximately 1,000 words demonstrating a clear and comprehensive understanding of the national GBV/DV campaign context (ref. Terms of Reference Article 2.1 – Overall Objectives). The narrative must explain how the Contracting Authority’s briefs will be interpreted and translated into coherent campaign concepts, with specific reference to Terms of Reference Article 1.1 and 4.2.1 (Campaign Strategy and Pre Launch). (i) Methodology for interpreting briefs and translating them into strategic campaign themes. (5 marks) (ii) End-to-end progression from strategy insight and executional outputs (4 marks) (iii

d on the basis of the following: • Accuracy and depth of understanding of the GBV/DV strategic framework • Ability to translate Terms of Reference requirements into a structured, campaign approach • Quality and logic of the proposed rationale • Structured methodology from briefs → themes → execution • Clear alignment with the National Strategy]]></label> <threshold>1</threshold> <value/> </criterion> <criterion level="2" pos="2" id="17877278647823" mandatory="1" included-in-evaluation="1" weight="12" type="file"> <weighted-score/> <label><![CDATA[1.2 Risks and Assumptions - Mandatory The Economic Operator shall submit a detailed Risk and Mitigation Report of approximately 1,000 words outlining key risks and mitigation measures relating to planning and approvals, resource and deadline management, flexibility, quality assurance, language clarity, and confidentiality/data protection, in accordance with Terms of Reference Articles 4.1–4.3.
